methodological_rigor.justification: The study triangulates evidence across public human scRNA-seq (GSE160189/GSE182109), murine scRNA-seq (GSE236243), flow cytometry across multiple tumor models (CT2A, E0771, Yummer1.7) and cLCMV, bulk RNA-seq of sorted TIM3+ T cells, TNFR2-KO mice, adoptive transfer of mixed WT/KO TRP2-TCR cells (internal controls), CD8 depletion to establish T-cell dependence, pharmacologic antagonism, and rechallenge for memory — a rigorous multi-model design. Statistics are appropriate: DESeq2 with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR, two-way repeated-measures ANOVA for tumor growth, Kaplan–Meier with log-rank, and explicit Bonferroni-style corrected α for multiple survival comparisons (0.05/6 = 0.00833). Weaknesses: no a priori power calculation is reported, randomization and blinded scoring are not described, mechanistic linkage of TNFR2 → TOX remains correlative (no rescue or signaling perturbation beyond KO/antagonist), and the melanoma model (Yummer1.7) did not show tumor control despite TNFR2 expression — a discrepancy acknowledged but not fully resolved.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study using murine tumor and chronic viral infection models with a human scRNA-seq reanalysis for context, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Clinical/translational relevance is nonetheless high: the paper identifies TNFR2 as an upstream regulator of TOX in exhaustion, tests a tool pharmacologic antagonist in combination with anti–PD-1, demonstrates efficacy in a translationally meaningful intracranial GBM (CT2A-Trp2) model with 55% long-term survival, and shows durable memory on rechallenge. Given the paucity of effective immunotherapy for GBM and the direct ICI-combination result, the findings offer a credible path to a first-in-human combination strategy and inform the biology of ICI resistance.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE is the applicable standard for this preclinical mouse study. Reporting is thorough on animal strains (RRIDs for all three strains), husbandry, housing, IACUC approval (A163-21-08), tumor implantation technique, humane endpoints (volume, size, ulceration), sample sizes per group (often N stated in captions, e.g., 19–20 per combo arm), antibodies with catalog/clone/RRID in Table 1, and statistical analysis. Gaps relative to ARRIVE: randomization method, allocation concealment, blinded outcome assessment, and a priori sample-size justification are not reported. Data availability is strong — raw FASTQs deposited at GEO GSE297330 and custom R scripts stated to be available (links redacted in the blinded version), with public datasets (GSE160189, GSE182109, GSE236243) explicitly identified.

novelty_literature.justification: The conceptual novelty is placing TNFR2 upstream of TOX during the Tex_prog→Tex_term transition and identifying a previously undescribed PD-1+TIM3+TOXlo population in TNFR2-deficient T cells with mixed progenitor/terminal functional features. Prior work has examined TNFR2 as a cancer target (refs. 34–35) and TNFR2 agonism in Tregs/autoimmunity (ref. 38), but the specific CD8-intrinsic role in exhaustion progression, the uncoupling of TIM3 from TOX, and the combination with checkpoint blockade across subcutaneous and intracranial tumors are novel contributions. Positioning in the literature is adequate — upstream regulators (NFAT, NR4A), TAM-driven exhaustion (ref. 24, from the same group), and prior TNF-exhaustion links (refs. 30–32) are appropriately cited; the gap argument is credible without over-claiming.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with a logical flow from scRNA-seq discovery → flow validation → functional phenotyping → KO/adoptive transfer → bulk transcriptomics → in vivo therapy. The abstract is quantitatively grounded and faithfully reflects the body. Figure legends are detailed and standalone-interpretable, with explicit statistical tests, time points, and corrected α values. Minor issues: a few typographic inconsistencies (e.g., 'Nfact3' vs 'Nfatc3'; 'lymphocyet'), the Discussion is somewhat repetitive of the Results in places, and the handling of the Yummer discrepancy and the gp33 granzyme B non-replication could be tightened.

key_strengths: Multi-model triangulation across three syngeneic tumor models, intracranial and subcutaneous compartments, and cLCMV chronic infection, with concordant findings
Clean genetic (TNFR2-KO) plus pharmacologic (anti-TNFR2 antagonist) complementarity, reinforced by mixed-chimera adoptive transfer isolating a T-cell-intrinsic effect
Translational payoff: anti-PD-1 + anti-TNFR2 combination yields 55% long-term survival in intracranial CT2A-Trp2 and durable memory on rechallenge
Novel description of a PD-1+TIM3+TOXlo population uncoupling TIM3 from TOX, supported by bulk RNA-seq showing diminished exhaustion program and enhanced AP1 signatures
Strong data sharing (GEO GSE297330) and explicit multiplicity correction for survival comparisons (α = 0.05/6)
key_concerns: Mechanistic linkage TNFR2 → NF-κB/NFAT → TOX remains correlative; no direct signaling perturbation or rescue experiment
Yummer1.7 melanoma expresses TNFR2 but TNFR2-KO mice do not control it — discrepancy acknowledged but not mechanistically resolved
ARRIVE items for randomization, blinding of outcome assessment, and a priori sample-size justification are not reported
Memory/effector interpretation of the TOXlo population is internally conflicted (lacks KLRG1/CD127 yet confers rechallenge immunity) and would benefit from epigenetic profiling
The gp33 physiologic re-stimulation did not reproduce the granzyme B increase seen with PMA/ionomycin, modestly tempering the cytotoxicity claim
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically strong, mechanistically novel preclinical immuno-oncology study with a credible translational combination therapy result in a GBM model, well short of Tier 1 practice-changing status given the correlative mechanism and one discordant tumor model, but comfortably within Tier 2 (e.g., JITC/JECCR-caliber) with minor revisions addressing reporting gaps and the Yummer/gp33 discrepancies.
